
### GRE packet format 

![](/encap/texfig/gre.figure-1.svg){fig-alt="GRE packet: IP or UDP header, then flag bits: C (checksum), 0 (fixed value), K (key), S (sequence number). Then fixed 0 value. Then version number 0. Then protocol type (ethertype value), then checksum (if C flag set), then 0 padding if C set, then key if K set, then sequence number if S set., then encapsulated data (which is usually IPv4 or IPv6)"}

### GRE packet format (flags)

![](/encap/texfig/gre.figure-2.svg){fig-alt="Same diagram as previous slide, with C, K, S bits highlighted"}

::: {.myoverbox .vlow}

*  checksum, "key" (basically port number), sequence number optional
*  bit in header indicates when present

:::

### GRE keys

![](/encap/texfig/gre.figure-3.svg){fig-alt="Same diagram as previous slide, with K flag bit and key highlighted."}


::: {.myoverbox .vlow}

*  key to allow multiple connections between IPs
*  if over UDP, could use separate ports instead/in addition
   *  but GRE most commonly used directly over IP

:::
